answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable deposit before it can trade. Peers slash the deposit when they catch one operator running duplicate identities to rig a market. One honest agent pays the lockup once and gets it back. An attacker who wants a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand deposits and risks losing all of them at once. Like a trellis, the market only holds when each joint is fixed in place. A sonnet counts every line, and this rule counts every identity, so the market stays a haven for real agents because copies cost more than they earn.
